---
title: "`panzoom` on every figure"
engine: jupyter
jupyter: python3
format:
  html:
    code-tools: true
filters:
  - path: ../../_filters/show-source.lua
    at: pre-ast
  - panzoom
panzoom: true
lightbox: true
---

panzoom takes every Python (Jupyter) figure lightbox would take on its own, so
no figure needs to be marked. lightbox is on too, but only [cells that ask for
it](#c4) with lightbox options open in it. The same cases open in lightbox alone
on [lightbox on the Python cases](j-jupyter-lightbox.html), and the R cases are
on [panzoom on every figure](c-panzoom-auto.html).

```yaml
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom: true
lightbox: true
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown on the
page. The **Code** button at the top shows the full source.

The plots share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## Figure with a caption {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

A Python figure with a caption. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## Plot without a caption {#c2 expect-open="panzoom"}

A plot without a caption. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## Subfigures {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

One cell with two plots, made subfigures by `fig-subcap`. Either one opens in
panzoom, in a two-image gallery.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave and a cosine wave, sin(2x) and cos(2x)."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| layout-ncol: 2

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## lightbox options {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

One cell with two plots and `lightbox:` options for a group and a description.
Asking for lightbox keeps the cell out of panzoom, as in cases 6 and 7 of
[panzoom on every figure](c-panzoom-auto.html). With Jupyter, lightbox ignores
these options, so each plot opens in lightbox on its own, without the group or
description.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by lightbox with Jupyter."
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## lightbox off {#c5 expect-open="nothing"}

A cell with `lightbox: false`. panzoom leaves a cell's own lightbox setting
alone, so clicking the plot does nothing.

```{python}
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave, sin(4x)."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## panzoom on a cell {#c6 expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with `#| panzoom: true`. It opens in panzoom, ahead of the document's
`lightbox: true`.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A cosine wave, cos(4x)."

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## Markdown image {#c7 expect-open="panzoom"}

A markdown image alone in a paragraph. It opens in panzoom.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Sunset at Chilmark Beach, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## Opt out of lightbox {#c8 expect-open="nothing"}

A markdown image with `.nolightbox`. panzoom only takes images lightbox would,
so clicking it does nothing.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Waves breaking below the clay cliffs at Aquinnah, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.nolightbox fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}
```
